name: Moonwell (Ashenvale)
summary: This secluded shrine, known to the night elves as the Moonwell of Purity, rests in central Ashenvale east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat. Its blessed waters channel the grace of Elune to nourish the ancient forest and cleanse creeping foulness from the land. Alliance travelers following Raene Wolfrunner's research often seek out Shael'dryn, who keeps watch beside its tranquil basin.

sections.title: Sanctuary of Purity
sections.body: Tucked away beneath the canopy of central Ashenvale, this moonwell serves as a spiritual anchor for the kaldorei. Its luminescent waters tap into nature's latent magic and the light of the Moon Goddess. As the surrounding forest suffers from satyr corruption, fel taint, and logging incursions, pure shrines like this one become vital lifelines for those trying to heal the woods.

sections.title: Healing the Wood
sections.body: Adventurers aiding Raene Wolfrunner come here to find Shael'dryn, who knows of the rod Dartol once created. She points them toward its scattered pieces and, once they are recovered, reconstructs the rod at the moonwell.

faq.q: What is this specific moonwell called?
faq.answer: This site is known as the Moonwell of Purity. It is one of several moonwells across Ashenvale, located east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat.

Moonwells are sacred basins consecrated to Elune that blend lunar power with natural magic. Night elves use them to sustain the land, replenish their spiritual strength, and purify items tainted by dark or demonic influences.

faq.q: Why do Alliance adventurers visit this moonwell?
faq.answer: Alliance heroes following Raene Wolfrunner's research out of Astranaar come here to seek Shael'dryn, who helps them recover the scattered pieces of Dartol's rod.

angles.text: Every moonwell is a sacred home away from home for the kaldorei, serving as both a spiritual font of Elune's grace and a frontline bulwark against the demonic taint threatening Ashenvale.
Tailors can harness the dense lunar energies pooling within the waters to weave pure Mooncloth from felcloth.
